notes: BOOK BANK CHARGES AND INTEREST STRAIGHT FROM THE RECONCILIATION. Before this release, a bank charge you had not yet recorded could be typed into Other adjustments, the difference driven to zero, and the month signed off — while your ledger still had no charge, the bank account was still overstated by it, and the expense never reached your Income and Expenditure. And you had to retype that same adjustment every single month, because the thing it made up for was never recorded. Each adjustment row now carries the account it belongs to and a BOOK button. Press it and the entry is posted on the STATEMENT DATE — a charge to the expense account you choose, interest to the income account — and the row disappears. Once it is in the ledger, no adjustment is needed. YOUR RECONCILIATION DOES NOT MOVE WHEN YOU BOOK: the cashbook shifts by exactly the amount the adjustment was supplying, so a month that balanced still balances, and you can do this in the middle of reconciling without losing your place. A genuine bank ERROR still belongs in Other adjustments — the bank will reverse it and there is nothing for you to record. The screen now explains which is which. THE SIGN GUIDANCE WAS WRONG, AND IS CORRECTED. The rule: a positive adjustment increases the statement toward the cashbook, a negative one decreases it. The hint underneath then said the opposite — that unbooked bank charges are "usually negative". They are POSITIVE: the bank has taken money your cashbook still shows. Interest not yet booked is NEGATIVE. Anyone following the old hint drove their difference further out and then went hunting for a mistake that was ours. Nothing else changed in this release.
